en.targetTerm: santa marta travel guide
en.titulo: Santa Marta guide: Tayrona Park, Teyuna and when it closes
en.enBreve: Santa Marta is organized around two outings: Tayrona National Natural Park and the Teyuna archaeological park, in the Sierra Nevada. Tayrona closes three times a year under agreements with the Indigenous peoples, and its fees changed in January 2026, according to [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/colombia/2026/01/07/parque-tayrona-ajusto-sus-tarifas-para-2026-asi-quedaron-los-precios-por-temporada-edad-y-tipo-de-visitante/). Check the dates before buying flights.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to enter Tayrona Park?
sections.answer: Walk-in admission for non-resident foreigners is 81,000 pesos in low season and 96,500 in high season; for Colombians and residents aged 25 and over, 36,500 and 43,000, according to [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/colombia/2026/01/07/parque-tayrona-ajusto-sus-tarifas-para-2026-asi-quedaron-los-precios-por-temporada-edad-y-tipo-de-visitante/), which cites Resolution 551 of 19 December 2025.
body: Colombians and residents under 25 pay 27,500 pesos in low season and 30,500 in high season, and the Bahía Concha sector has separate fees, details the same [Infobae article](https://www.infobae.com/colombia/2026/01/07/parque-tayrona-ajusto-sus-tarifas-para-2026-asi-quedaron-los-precios-por-temporada-edad-y-tipo-de-visitante/). A car entry costs 21,000 pesos and a motorcycle 14,500.
Bring cash and plan the transfer from the city: the entrances are on the highway, far from the town, and inside almost the entire route is on foot.

sections.h2: When does Tayrona Park close?
sections.answer: From 1 to 15 February, from 1 to 15 June and from 19 October to 2 November, for the periods of retreat agreed with the peoples who live in the territory, according to [Infobae](https://www.infobae.com/colombia/2026/01/07/parque-tayrona-ajusto-sus-tarifas-para-2026-asi-quedaron-los-precios-por-temporada-edad-y-tipo-de-visitante/).
body: If your trip falls in those weeks, move your park day or change plans: the closure applies to tourist visits, not to the city, which keeps running as usual.
Before paying for accommodation in the beach area, check that your dates don't fall within one of those periods.

sections.h2: What is Teyuna or the Lost City?
sections.answer: An archaeological park in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, within the Kogui-Malayo-Arhuaco reserve, open from 7:00 to 15:00, according to the [ICANH](https://icanh.gov.co/investigacion/recursos-para-investigacion/publicaciones/colecciones/guias-turisticas-los-parques-arqueologicos-nacionales/teyuna-ciudad-perdida-1).
body: The site was officially made known in 1976 and the [ICANH](https://icanh.gov.co/investigacion/recursos-para-investigacion/publicaciones/colecciones/guias-turisticas-los-parques-arqueologicos-nacionales/teyuna-ciudad-perdida-1) itself acknowledges that little is still known about the Tairona.
The visit isn't a morning outing: it means hiking several days through the sierra, so it's prepared well in advance and with your physical condition in mind.

titulo: Guía de Lhasa: Palacio Potala, permiso del Tíbet y altura
author: editorial
enBreve: Lhasa pide dos preparativos antes que nada: el permiso para entrar al Tíbet y un par de días para aclimatarse, porque el Palacio Potala está a unos 3,700 metros, según la [UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/707/). El palacio cierra los lunes desde el 1 de diciembre, informó [China Services Info](https://www.chinaservicesinfo.com/s/202511/18/WS691bcaa4498e368550337a6f/lhasas-potala-palace-to-implement-monday-closure-policy_2.html).

sections.h2: ¿Qué es el conjunto del Palacio Potala?
sections.answer: El palacio de invierno del Dalái Lama, sobre la Montaña Roja, en el centro del valle de Lhasa, a unos 3,700 metros de altura; la [UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/707/) lo inscribió en 1994.
body: El conjunto suma después el templo de Jokhang, un complejo de 2.5 hectáreas en el casco antiguo, y Norbulingka, el palacio de verano con jardines de 36 hectáreas, según la misma [ficha de la UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/707/).
Son tres visitas distintas y conviene repartirlas en días diferentes, sobre todo en los primeros días, cuando el cuerpo todavía se está acostumbrando a la altura.

sections.h2: ¿Qué días y horas abre el Palacio Potala?
sections.answer: De martes a domingo: de 9:00 a 15:40 del 1 de mayo al 31 de octubre, y de 9:30 a 15:20 del 1 de noviembre al 30 de abril, con cierre los lunes a partir del 1 de diciembre, según [China Services Info](https://www.chinaservicesinfo.com/s/202511/18/WS691bcaa4498e368550337a6f/lhasas-potala-palace-to-implement-monday-closure-policy_2.html).
body: La misma [nota](https://www.chinaservicesinfo.com/s/202511/18/WS691bcaa4498e368550337a6f/lhasas-potala-palace-to-implement-monday-closure-policy_2.html) solo pide planear el viaje con ese calendario en mente. Confirma el horario poco antes de ir, porque el cierre de los lunes es reciente.

sections.h2: ¿Qué se necesita para viajar al Tíbet?
sections.answer: Además de la visa de China, un permiso para entrar al Tíbet, que se tramita con una agencia especializada del país, y viajar en un recorrido organizado, según el [gobierno del Reino Unido](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/china/regional-risks).
body: La misma [página oficial](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/china/regional-risks) advierte que las autoridades chinas a veces dejan de expedir permisos sin aviso y que en los monasterios budistas hay que pedir autorización antes de tomar fotografías.
Resuelve el trámite antes de comprar vuelos: es lo que ordena el resto del viaje.

en.titulo: Lhasa guide: Potala Palace, the Tibet permit and altitude
en.enBreve: Lhasa calls for two preparations before anything else: the permit to enter Tibet and a couple of days to acclimatize, because the Potala Palace stands at about 3,700 meters, according to [UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/707/). The palace closes on Mondays from 1 December, reported [China Services Info](https://www.chinaservicesinfo.com/s/202511/18/WS691bcaa4498e368550337a6f/lhasas-potala-palace-to-implement-monday-closure-policy_2.html).

sections.h2: What is the Potala Palace ensemble?
sections.answer: The Dalai Lama's winter palace, on Red Mountain in the center of the Lhasa valley, at about 3,700 meters above sea level; [UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/707/) inscribed it in 1994.
body: The ensemble later added the Jokhang Temple, a 2.5-hectare complex in the old town, and Norbulingka, the summer palace with 36 hectares of gardens, according to the same [UNESCO listing](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/707/).
They're three separate visits and it's best to spread them over different days, especially in the first days, when your body is still getting used to the altitude.

sections.h2: What days and hours is the Potala Palace open?
sections.answer: Tuesday to Sunday: from 9:00 to 15:40 from 1 May to 31 October, and from 9:30 to 15:20 from 1 November to 30 April, closing on Mondays from 1 December, according to [China Services Info](https://www.chinaservicesinfo.com/s/202511/18/WS691bcaa4498e368550337a6f/lhasas-potala-palace-to-implement-monday-closure-policy_2.html).
body: The same [article](https://www.chinaservicesinfo.com/s/202511/18/WS691bcaa4498e368550337a6f/lhasas-potala-palace-to-implement-monday-closure-policy_2.html) only asks visitors to plan their trip with that schedule in mind. Confirm the hours shortly before you go, because the Monday closure is recent.

sections.h2: What do you need to travel to Tibet?
sections.answer: In addition to a Chinese visa, a permit to enter Tibet, arranged through a specialized agency in the country, and traveling on an organized tour, according to the [UK government](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/china/regional-risks).
body: The same [official page](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/china/regional-risks) warns that the Chinese authorities sometimes stop issuing permits without notice and that in Buddhist monasteries you must ask permission before taking photographs.
Sort out the paperwork before buying flights: it's what shapes the rest of the trip.

titulo: Guía de Chongqing: las tallas de Dazu, horarios y entradas
author: editorial
enBreve: La salida grande de Chongqing son las tallas rupestres de Dazu, en el distrito del mismo nombre: 75 sitios protegidos y más de 50,000 estatuas, según el [Gobierno de Chongqing](https://english.cq.gov.cn/aboutchongqing/culture/CulturalHeritage/202606/t20260612_15751040.html), que las ubica en la lista de Patrimonio Mundial desde diciembre de 1999. Calcula un día completo, porque quedan fuera de la ciudad.

sections.h2: ¿Qué son las tallas rupestres de Dazu?
sections.answer: Cinco conjuntos de tallas en roca de los siglos IX al XIII, con temas de budismo tántrico, taoísmo y confucianismo junto a escenas de la vida cotidiana, según la [UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/912/).
body: El [Gobierno de Chongqing](https://english.cq.gov.cn/aboutchongqing/culture/CulturalHeritage/202606/t20260612_15751040.html) cuenta 75 sitios protegidos y más de 50,000 estatuas, repartidos en conjuntos como Beishan, Baodingshan, Nanshan, Shimenshan y Shizhuanshan, con tallas que arrancan al inicio de la dinastía Tang y siguen hasta Ming y Qing.
No se recorren todos en una visita: Baodingshan y Beishan son los dos conjuntos que suelen verse juntos en una misma jornada.

sections.h2: ¿Qué horario y qué precio tienen?
sections.answer: El [Gobierno de Chongqing](https://english.cq.gov.cn/aboutchongqing/culture/CulturalHeritage/202606/t20260612_15751040.html) indica horario de 8:30 a 17:30 en Beishan Road; [China Daily](https://govt.chinadaily.com.cn/s/201812/17/WS5d074398498e12256565dcdc/dazu-rock-carvings-chongqing.html) daba 140 yuanes en temporada alta, del 1 de febrero al 30 de noviembre, y 120 yuanes el resto del año.
body: Esa [página de China Daily](https://govt.chinadaily.com.cn/s/201812/17/WS5d074398498e12256565dcdc/dazu-rock-carvings-chongqing.html) se actualizó en diciembre de 2018 y menciona también guía en inglés por 260 yuanes, así que confirma la tarifa antes de ir.

sections.h2: ¿Cómo se organiza un día en Chongqing?
sections.answer: Deja la salida a Dazu en un día completo y reserva el resto del tiempo para la ciudad, que está construida sobre colinas y se camina despacio.
body: Si llegas en tren o en avión por la mañana, ese primer día sirve para ubicarte y dejar las tallas para el siguiente, ya con el traslado resuelto.

en.targetTerm: chongqing travel guide
en.titulo: Chongqing guide: the Dazu carvings, opening hours and tickets
en.enBreve: Chongqing's big outing is the Dazu rock carvings, in the district of the same name: 75 protected sites and more than 50,000 statues, according to the [Chongqing Government](https://english.cq.gov.cn/aboutchongqing/culture/CulturalHeritage/202606/t20260612_15751040.html), which notes they've been on the World Heritage list since December 1999. Allow a full day, because they're outside the city.

sections.h2: What are the Dazu rock carvings?
sections.answer: Five groups of rock carvings from the 9th to the 13th centuries, with themes from Tantric Buddhism, Taoism and Confucianism alongside scenes of everyday life, according to [UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/912/).
body: The [Chongqing Government](https://english.cq.gov.cn/aboutchongqing/culture/CulturalHeritage/202606/t20260612_15751040.html) counts 75 protected sites and more than 50,000 statues, spread across groups such as Beishan, Baodingshan, Nanshan, Shimenshan and Shizhuanshan, with carvings that begin in the early Tang dynasty and continue through the Ming and Qing.
You can't see them all in one visit: Baodingshan and Beishan are the two groups usually seen together in the same day.

sections.h2: What are the opening hours and prices?
sections.answer: The [Chongqing Government](https://english.cq.gov.cn/aboutchongqing/culture/CulturalHeritage/202606/t20260612_15751040.html) lists hours from 8:30 to 17:30 on Beishan Road; [China Daily](https://govt.chinadaily.com.cn/s/201812/17/WS5d074398498e12256565dcdc/dazu-rock-carvings-chongqing.html) gave 140 yuan in high season, from 1 February to 30 November, and 120 yuan the rest of the year.
body: That [China Daily page](https://govt.chinadaily.com.cn/s/201812/17/WS5d074398498e12256565dcdc/dazu-rock-carvings-chongqing.html) was updated in December 2018 and also mentions an English-speaking guide for 260 yuan, so confirm the price before you go.

sections.h2: Where is Bhaktapur, and what is it like?
sections.answer: It is a medieval city about 14 kilometres east of Kathmandu, according to [In Your Pocket](https://www.inyourpocket.com/nepal/kathmandu/articles/a-guide-to-the-unesco-world-heritage-sites-of-the). Its streets are paved with brick and its historic centre is almost free of cars.
body: The guide calls it the showpiece of the valley and says it is far better preserved than Kathmandu, with Newari woodcarving among the finest anywhere. The city is one of the seven UNESCO World Heritage Sites in the Kathmandu Valley, according to the [same guide](https://www.inyourpocket.com/nepal/kathmandu/articles/a-guide-to-the-unesco-world-heritage-sites-of-the), and the whole valley was designated in 1979, per [Encounters Travel](https://www.encounterstravel.com/blog/bhaktapur).

sections.h2: What is there to see on Durbar Square?
sections.answer: The 55-Window Palace is its centrepiece. It is a 15th-century royal palace, and its carved windows are among the finest examples of Newari woodcarving, according to [In Your Pocket](https://www.inyourpocket.com/nepal/kathmandu/articles/a-guide-to-the-unesco-world-heritage-sites-of-the).
body: The main entrance to the square is the Lion's Gate, also called Singha Durbar, according to [Encounters Travel](https://www.encounterstravel.com/blog/bhaktapur). Once inside, give yourself time to walk past the temples and palaces at your own pace.

Nearby, Taumadhi Square holds the Nyatapola Temple, a five-storey pagoda dating from 1702 that came through the 2015 earthquake almost unscathed, according to [In Your Pocket](https://www.inyourpocket.com/nepal/kathmandu/articles/a-guide-to-the-unesco-world-heritage-sites-of-the).

sections.h2: How much is the entrance, and what does it cover?
sections.answer: For foreigners it costs US$18 or NPR 1,800. The ticket covers Durbar Square, Taumadhi Square, Dattatreya Square and the historic area around them, according to [In Your Pocket](https://www.inyourpocket.com/nepal/kathmandu/articles/a-guide-to-the-unesco-world-heritage-sites-of-the).
body: The ticket is valid for several visits over several consecutive days, and children under 10 enter free, according to the [same guide](https://www.inyourpocket.com/nepal/kathmandu/articles/a-guide-to-the-unesco-world-heritage-sites-of-the). Fees can change, so confirm them before you travel.
The 55-Window Palace is usually included in the square ticket, so you do not need to pay for it separately, per [Encounters Travel](https://www.encounterstravel.com/blog/bhaktapur).

sections.h2: When should you go?
sections.answer: Go early: the square is typically open from about 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM, according to [Encounters Travel](https://www.encounterstravel.com/blog/bhaktapur).
body: In the morning you can watch potters at work in Pottery Square, where traditional techniques have been kept for centuries, the same source notes. Avoid midday, when the heat is strongest.
For photographing the carved windows in good light, mid-morning and early afternoon are good moments.

Bring cash for the ticket, comfortable shoes for the paved streets and water; the historic centre is best explored on foot.

body: UNESCO describes the rock as a granite peak that dominates the jungle around it, and the site entrance is marked by a gigantic lion made of brick and plaster, per the [UNESCO page](https://whc.unesco.org/en/documents/124445).

sections.h2: What are the painted maidens?
sections.answer: They are frescoes of adorned female figures on the western face of the rock, halfway up. Only 22 survive, out of the hundreds that once existed, according to the [Central Cultural Fund](https://ccf.gov.lk/heritage-sites/sigiriya-rock-fortress/).
body: They are sheltered in a shallow recess in the rock. Scholars interpret them as apsaras, queens or consorts, or goddesses, and the same [Central Cultural Fund page](https://ccf.gov.lk/heritage-sites/sigiriya-rock-fortress/) explains this, so read the on-site explanation before you climb.

sections.h2: What is the mirror wall?
sections.answer: It is a wall below the frescoes that was once finished with highly polished lime plaster. Between the 6th and 14th centuries visitors scratched poems and reflections into it, according to the [Central Cultural Fund](https://ccf.gov.lk/heritage-sites/sigiriya-rock-fortress/).
body: More than 1,800 inscriptions have been documented, per the [same source](https://ccf.gov.lk/heritage-sites/sigiriya-rock-fortress/), which shows the site kept drawing visitors for centuries after it was built.

sections.h2: How long does the climb take, and when should you go?
sections.answer: The ascent takes 1.5 to 2 hours and involves about 1,200 steps, according to the [Central Cultural Fund](https://ccf.gov.lk/heritage-sites/sigiriya-rock-fortress/).
body: Early morning or late afternoon is recommended for cooler temperatures, per the same source. Bring water, comfortable shoes and time to rest on the steeper sections.
We could not confirm opening hours or ticket prices from the official source we checked, so confirm them before you travel.

sections.h2: How to plan your visit
sections.answer: Sigiriya can be combined with other stops in central Sri Lanka. Browse [Travel Puzzle tours](/tours) and compare [destinations](/destinos) on the island before choosing your route.
body: The visit to the rock and the archaeological site can take a good part of the day, so start early and follow the staff's instructions.
Do not touch the paintings or the inscriptions; they are fragile and are part of what gives the site its value.

author: editorial
enBreve: Kandy fue sede del reino kandiano desde 1592 hasta que tropas británicas entraron en 1815, según la [UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/document/163325). Su centro sagrado, con el Templo del Diente, es Patrimonio Mundial desde 1988. Para entrar al templo cubre hombros y rodillas y quítate los zapatos, según el [Centro Cultural Nacional de Sri Lanka](https://ccf.gov.lk/heritage-sites/temple-of-the-tooth/).

sections.h2: ¿Por qué Kandy es tan importante?
sections.answer: Se convirtió en capital del reino en 1592 y fue el último centro de la monarquía en la isla, según la [UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/document/163325).
body: Las tropas británicas entraron a la ciudad el 14 de febrero de 1815, de acuerdo con la misma [página de la UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/document/163325). El complejo del templo se construyó sobre todo durante la época del reino, entre 1592 y 1815, según el [Centro Cultural Nacional](https://ccf.gov.lk/heritage-sites/temple-of-the-tooth/).

sections.h2: ¿Qué es el Templo del Diente?
sections.answer: Es el templo que guarda la reliquia del diente de Buda, muy venerada, según la [UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/document/163325). Según el [Centro Cultural Nacional](https://ccf.gov.lk/heritage-sites/temple-of-the-tooth/), la reliquia llegó a Kandy en 1595.
body: La tradición dice que la reliquia se tomó de la pira funeraria de Buda en Kushinagar en 543 antes de nuestra era, y que llegó a Sri Lanka en el siglo IV, según el [Centro Cultural Nacional](https://ccf.gov.lk/heritage-sites/temple-of-the-tooth/).
Un atentado con bomba en 1998 dañó gravemente el templo, que después fue restaurado por completo, según la [UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/document/163325).

sections.h2: ¿Cuándo se celebra la gran procesión?
sections.answer: El Esala Perahera se celebra en julio o agosto y dura diez noches, con su momento culminante en el Randoli Perahera, según el [Centro Cultural Nacional](https://ccf.gov.lk/heritage-sites/temple-of-the-tooth/).
body: En esa procesión, un cofre dorado que se cree contiene la reliquia del diente va sobre un elefante decorado por las calles de Kandy. La celebración también honra a cuatro deidades guardianas: Natha, Vishnu, Kataragama y Pattini, según la misma fuente.

sections.h2: ¿Cómo debes vestirte y comportarte en el templo?
sections.answer: Cubre hombros y rodillas, y quítate los zapatos al entrar, según el [Centro Cultural Nacional](https://ccf.gov.lk/heritage-sites/temple-of-the-tooth/).
body: Hay tres ceremonias diarias, al amanecer, al mediodía y al atardecer, según la misma fuente, aunque no indica las horas exactas. Confírmalas en el lugar antes de ir.
Los horarios de apertura y el precio para extranjeros no aparecen en las páginas oficiales que revisamos, así que confírmalos antes de viajar.

en.titulo: Kandy: the Temple of the Tooth and Sri Lanka's last royal seat
en.enBreve: Kandy was the seat of the Kandyan kingdom from 1592 until British troops entered in 1815, according to [UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/document/163325). Its sacred city, with the Temple of the Tooth, has been a World Heritage site since 1988. To enter the temple, cover your shoulders and knees and remove your shoes, per the [Central Cultural Fund](https://ccf.gov.lk/heritage-sites/temple-of-the-tooth/).

sections.h2: Why is Kandy so important?
sections.answer: It became the capital of the kingdom in 1592 and was the last seat of royal power on the island, according to [UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/document/163325).
body: British troops entered the city on 14 February 1815, per the same [UNESCO page](https://whc.unesco.org/document/163325). The temple complex was built mainly during the Kandyan era, from 1592 to 1815, according to the [Central Cultural Fund](https://ccf.gov.lk/heritage-sites/temple-of-the-tooth/).

sections.h2: What is the Temple of the Tooth?
sections.answer: It houses the relic of the Buddha's tooth, which has long been greatly venerated, according to [UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/document/163325). The relic moved to Kandy in 1595, per the [Central Cultural Fund](https://ccf.gov.lk/heritage-sites/temple-of-the-tooth/).
body: Tradition holds that the relic was taken from the Buddha's funeral pyre in Kushinagar in 543 BCE and reached Sri Lanka in the 4th century CE, according to the [Central Cultural Fund](https://ccf.gov.lk/heritage-sites/temple-of-the-tooth/).
A terrorist bomb blast in 1998 caused serious damage to the temple, which was then fully restored, according to [UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/document/163325).

sections.h2: When is the great procession?
sections.answer: The Esala Perahera takes place in July or August and lasts ten nights, peaking in the Randoli Perahera, according to the [Central Cultural Fund](https://ccf.gov.lk/heritage-sites/temple-of-the-tooth/).
body: A golden casket, believed to hold the tooth relic, is carried through the streets on a decorated elephant. The procession also honours four guardian deities: Natha, Vishnu, Kataragama and Pattini, per the same [source](https://ccf.gov.lk/heritage-sites/temple-of-the-tooth/).

sections.h2: How should you dress and behave at the temple?
sections.answer: Cover your shoulders and knees, and remove your shoes on entry, according to the [Central Cultural Fund](https://ccf.gov.lk/heritage-sites/temple-of-the-tooth/).
body: Three daily ceremonies take place at dawn, noon and evening, per the same source, though it does not give exact times, so confirm them locally.
We could not find opening hours or foreigner ticket prices on the official pages we checked, so confirm them before you travel.

sections.h2: How to plan your visit
sections.answer: Kandy can be combined with other stops on the island. Browse [Travel Puzzle tours](/tours) and compare [destinations](/destinos) in Sri Lanka before choosing your route.
body: A visit to the temple can take a good part of the morning or afternoon, so arrive early enough to watch the ceremonies without rushing.

author: editorial
enBreve: El fuerte de Galle es Patrimonio Mundial de la UNESCO desde 1988, según [Ceylon Expeditions](https://www.ceylonexpeditions.com/galle-dutch-fort-sri-lanka). Los holandeses lo tomaron en 1640 y comenzaron una gran reconstrucción en 1649. Sus 14 bastiones y la muralla de unos 2 kilómetros se pueden recorrer a pie, según [Wonders of Ceylon](https://www.wondersofceylon.com/galle-fort).

sections.h2: ¿Quién construyó el fuerte?
sections.answer: Los portugueses llegaron en 1505 y levantaron un primer fuerte; los holandeses lo tomaron en 1640 y empezaron una gran obra de reconstrucción en 1649, según [Wonders of Ceylon](https://www.wondersofceylon.com/galle-fort).
body: Los británicos tomaron el control en 1796, según [Ceylon Expeditions](https://www.ceylonexpeditions.com/galle-dutch-fort-sri-lanka). Las fuentes no coinciden sobre cuándo se levantó el primer fuerte portugués, así que esta guía no da esa fecha.

sections.h2: ¿Qué se puede ver dentro?
sections.answer: El fuerte cubre 52 hectáreas dentro de sus muros y tiene 14 bastiones, según [Ceylon Expeditions](https://www.ceylonexpeditions.com/galle-dutch-fort-sri-lanka), con murallas de unos 2 kilómetros, según [Wonders of Ceylon](https://www.wondersofceylon.com/galle-fort).
body: Puedes caminar por las murallas y visitar el faro, que está sobre el bastión Utrecht, según [Ceylon Expeditions](https://www.ceylonexpeditions.com/galle-dutch-fort-sri-lanka).

Entre los edificios religiosos está la iglesia reformada holandesa, de 1775, y la mezquita Meeran Jumma, de 1904, construida sobre las ruinas de una capilla portuguesa, según [Wonders of Ceylon](https://www.wondersofceylon.com/galle-fort).

sections.h2: ¿Qué torre y qué museos hay?
sections.answer: Una torre se levantó en 1883 para el jubileo de la reina Victoria, y en el fuerte están el Museo Marítimo y el Museo Nacional de Galle, según [Ceylon Expeditions](https://www.ceylonexpeditions.com/galle-dutch-fort-sri-lanka).
body: La inscripción de la UNESCO cubre el casco antiguo de Galle y sus fortificaciones, y se hizo en 1988, según la misma página de [Ceylon Expeditions](https://www.ceylonexpeditions.com/galle-dutch-fort-sri-lanka).

sections.h2: ¿Qué conviene saber antes de ir?
sections.answer: Las fuentes que consultamos no indican precios de entrada ni horarios del fuerte, así que confírmalos en el lugar antes de viajar, según [Wonders of Ceylon](https://www.wondersofceylon.com/galle-fort).
body: Lleva agua y gorra, porque gran parte del recorrido por las murallas es al aire libre y con sol.

en.enBreve: Galle Fort has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1988, according to [Ceylon Expeditions](https://www.ceylonexpeditions.com/galle-dutch-fort-sri-lanka). The Dutch took it in 1640 and began a major rebuilding in 1649. Its 14 bastions and walls of about 2 kilometres can be walked, according to [Wonders of Ceylon](https://www.wondersofceylon.com/galle-fort).

sections.h2: Who built the fort?
sections.answer: The Portuguese arrived in 1505 and built an early fort; the Dutch captured it in 1640 and began a major rebuilding in 1649, according to [Wonders of Ceylon](https://www.wondersofceylon.com/galle-fort).
body: The British took control in 1796, per [Ceylon Expeditions](https://www.ceylonexpeditions.com/galle-dutch-fort-sri-lanka). The sources disagree on when the first Portuguese fort went up, so this guide does not give that date.

sections.h2: What can you see inside?
sections.answer: The fort covers 52 hectares inside its walls and has 14 bastions, according to [Ceylon Expeditions](https://www.ceylonexpeditions.com/galle-dutch-fort-sri-lanka), with walls about 2 kilometres long, per [Wonders of Ceylon](https://www.wondersofceylon.com/galle-fort).
body: You can walk along the ramparts and visit the lighthouse, which stands on the Utrecht bastion, according to [Ceylon Expeditions](https://www.ceylonexpeditions.com/galle-dutch-fort-sri-lanka).

Among the religious buildings are a Dutch Reformed church dating from 1775 and the Meeran Jumma Mosque, built in 1904 over the ruins of an earlier Portuguese chapel, per [Wonders of Ceylon](https://www.wondersofceylon.com/galle-fort).

sections.h2: Which tower and museums are there?
sections.answer: A tower was erected in 1883 for Queen Victoria's jubilee, and the fort hosts the Maritime Museum and the Galle National Museum, according to [Ceylon Expeditions](https://www.ceylonexpeditions.com/galle-dutch-fort-sri-lanka).
body: The UNESCO inscription covers the Old Town of Galle and its Fortifications, inscribed in 1988, as the same [Ceylon Expeditions page](https://www.ceylonexpeditions.com/galle-dutch-fort-sri-lanka) describes.

sections.h2: ¿Qué es el puente de los nueve arcos?
sections.answer: Es un puente de piedra de 90 metros con nueve arcos, que se ubica entre Ella y Demodara, según [22 Places](https://www.22places.com/ella-sri-lanka-travel-guide/) y [The Common Wanderer](https://www.thecommonwanderer.com/blog/things-to-do-ella-sri-lanka).

La misma guía advierte que el puente no tiene barandillas de seguridad, así que cuando escuches un tren, aléjate del paso, según [The Common Wanderer](https://www.thecommonwanderer.com/blog/things-to-do-ella-sri-lanka).

sections.h2: ¿Qué caminatas puedes hacer desde Ella?

sections.h2: ¿Cuántos días conviene dedicar a Colombo?
sections.answer: Uno o dos días bastan para la ciudad, y el resto del viaje puedes usarlo para salir a otras partes de la isla. Es una ciudad para caminar por tramos cortos, con templos, un lago y barrios de mercado.
body: Según [Tripoto](https://www.tripoto.com/colombo/places-to-visit/gangaramaya-temple), Galle Face Green, el Colombo City Centre y el parque Viharamahadevi quedan a unos 2 o 3 kilómetros del templo Gangaramaya, así que puedes combinarlos en un mismo día.
Si llegas de noche, empieza con una cena cerca de Galle Face Green y deja las visitas para el día siguiente. La primera mañana puede ser para el templo, cuando hay menos gente.

sections.h2: ¿Cómo se visita el templo Gangaramaya?
sections.answer: El templo abre todos los días de 6:00 a 22:00 y cobra una entrada de 300 rupias de Sri Lanka por persona, según [Tripoto](https://www.tripoto.com/colombo/places-to-visit/gangaramaya-temple). La entrada incluye el templo, el museo, la biblioteca y el Seema Malaka.
body: Para entrar hay que cubrir hombros y rodillas, y quitarse los zapatos y los sombreros antes de pasar a las zonas de culto, indica [Eris Goes To](https://erisgoesto.com/2026/05/07/the-complete-visitors-guide-to-gangaramaya-temple-colombo-sri-lanka/). Dentro se ven un gran Buda en el santuario principal, el pabellón del Buda de jade y un árbol Bodhi sobre una plataforma en el patio.

La misma guía recomienda ir temprano, cuando hay menos visitantes, o hacia las 18:00 para la ceremonia vespertina con tambores. Las fotos suelen estar permitidas, pero conviene preguntar antes de retratar a monjes y devotos. [Eris Goes To](https://erisgoesto.com/2026/05/07/the-complete-visitors-guide-to-gangaramaya-temple-colombo-sri-lanka/)

sections.h2: ¿Cómo llegar desde el centro?

en.titulo: Colombo guide: temples, the lake and a walk through Sri Lanka's capital
en.enBreve: Colombo is the gateway to Sri Lanka and is easy to explore in one or two days. The Gangaramaya Temple, by Beira Lake, is open from 6:00 to 22:00 and charges 300 Sri Lankan rupees, according to [Tripoto](https://www.tripoto.com/colombo/places-to-visit/gangaramaya-temple). Visitors must cover their shoulders and knees to enter, according to [Eris Goes To](https://erisgoesto.com/2026/05/07/the-complete-visitors-guide-to-gangaramaya-temple-colombo-sri-lanka/).

sections.h2: How many days should you spend in Colombo?
sections.answer: One or two days are enough for the city, and you can use the rest of the trip to head out to other parts of the island. It is a city for walking short distances, with temples, a lake and market neighborhoods.
body: According to [Tripoto](https://www.tripoto.com/colombo/places-to-visit/gangaramaya-temple), Galle Face Green, Colombo City Centre and Viharamahadevi Park are each about 2 to 3 kilometers from the Gangaramaya Temple, so you can combine them in a single day.
If you arrive at night, start with dinner near Galle Face Green and leave the sights for the next day. Your first morning can go to the temple, when there are fewer people.

sections.h2: How do you visit the Gangaramaya Temple?
sections.answer: The temple opens every day from 6:00 to 22:00 and charges an entry fee of 300 Sri Lankan rupees per person, according to [Tripoto](https://www.tripoto.com/colombo/places-to-visit/gangaramaya-temple). The ticket covers the temple, the museum, the library and the Seema Malaka.
body: To enter, you need to cover your shoulders and knees and take off your shoes and hats before entering worship areas, says [Eris Goes To](https://erisgoesto.com/2026/05/07/the-complete-visitors-guide-to-gangaramaya-temple-colombo-sri-lanka/). Inside you will find a large Buddha statue in the main shrine, the Jade Buddha pavilion and a Bodhi tree on a raised platform in the courtyard.

The same guide recommends going early, when there are fewer visitors, or around 18:00 for the evening pooja with traditional drumming. Photography is generally allowed, but it is wise to ask before photographing monks and devotees. [Eris Goes To](https://erisgoesto.com/2026/05/07/the-complete-visitors-guide-to-gangaramaya-temple-colombo-sri-lanka/)

sections.h2: How do you get there from the center?
sections.answer: The temple is on Jinaratana Road, near Beira Lake, and from Colombo Fort or Pettah you can reach it by bus, train, taxi or tuk-tuk, according to [Tripoto](https://www.tripoto.com/colombo/places-to-visit/gangaramaya-temple).
body: A tuk-tuk ride takes about 10 to 15 minutes and a taxi about 15 to 20 minutes, with approximate fares of 150 to 300 rupees by tuk-tuk and 300 to 500 by taxi, says the same source. Uber and PickMe also work in the city. [Tripoto](https://www.tripoto.com/colombo/places-to-visit/gangaramaya-temple)
From the temple you can walk to the lake and then continue toward the center at a relaxed pace, without rushing through traffic.

author: editorial
enBreve: Bombay, también llamada Mumbai, se recorre bien en un día con la Puerta de la India y el barrio de Colaba. El monumento abre las 24 horas y la entrada es gratuita, según [Mumbai Metro Times](https://www.mumbaimetrotimes.com/places/gateway-of-india/). Desde sus muelles salen lanchas a las cuevas de Elefanta, a cerca de una hora de trayecto, según [Indiaesque](https://indiaesque.com/mumbai/heritage-guide).

sections.h2: ¿Qué ver primero en Bombay?
sections.answer: Empieza en la Puerta de la India, en Apollo Bandar, frente al hotel Taj Mahal Palace, y deja tiempo para caminar por Colaba. El monumento abre todo el día y la entrada es gratuita, según [Mumbai Metro Times](https://www.mumbaimetrotimes.com/places/gateway-of-india/).
body: La Puerta de la India se construyó entre 1915 y 1924 y se inauguró el 4 de diciembre de 1924. La diseñó el arquitecto escocés George Wittet para conmemorar la visita de 1911 de los reyes Jorge V y María, según [Mumbai Metro Times](https://www.mumbaimetrotimes.com/places/gateway-of-india/).

Indiaesque describe el monumento como un arco de piedra de estilo indo-sarraceno y advierte que siempre hay mucha gente, así que conviene ir temprano por la mañana para verlo con menos visitantes. Desde ahí se ven el puerto y el hotel Taj Mahal Palace. [Indiaesque](https://indiaesque.com/mumbai/heritage-guide)

sections.h2: ¿Cómo llegar a las cuevas de Elefanta?
sections.answer: Las lanchas salen de los muelles junto a la Puerta de la India y el cruce dura cerca de una hora por trayecto, según [Indiaesque](https://indiaesque.com/mumbai/heritage-guide).
body: Las cuevas, declaradas Patrimonio Mundial en 1987, tienen lanchas de las 9:00 a las 15:30, y están cerradas los lunes y durante el monzón, indica la misma fuente. Revisa el día antes de planear el viaje. [Indiaesque](https://indiaesque.com/mumbai/heritage-guide)

Las fuentes consultadas no nombran a las empresas de lanchas, así que conviene confirmar en el muelle cuál opera el día de tu visita. El viaje de ida y vuelta se ubica entre 150 y 250 rupias, según la misma guía. [Indiaesque](https://indiaesque.com/mumbai/heritage-guide)

sections.h2: ¿Cómo moverte desde el centro?
sections.answer: El metro más cercano es Hutatma Chowk, en la Línea 3 (Aqua Line), a unos 1.5 kilómetros de la Puerta, según [Mumbai Metro Times](https://www.mumbaimetrotimes.com/places/gateway-of-india/).
body: Los trenes locales de Churchgate y de CSMT quedan a unos 2 kilómetros, así que para muchos visitantes caminar o tomar un taxi desde esas estaciones resulta lo más sencillo. [Mumbai Metro Times](https://www.mumbaimetrotimes.com/places/gateway-of-india/)

La zona se concurre más de cinco a nueve de la noche, según la misma página, así que conviene planear el paseo por Colaba fuera de esa franja. [Mumbai Metro Times](https://www.mumbaimetrotimes.com/places/gateway-of-india/)

en.titulo: Mumbai guide: the Gateway of India, the Elephanta Caves and how to get around
en.enBreve: Mumbai, also known as Bombay, is easy to cover in a day with the Gateway of India and the Colaba neighborhood. The monument is open 24 hours and entry is free, according to [Mumbai Metro Times](https://www.mumbaimetrotimes.com/places/gateway-of-india/). Boats to the Elephanta Caves leave from its jetties, a crossing of about one hour, according to [Indiaesque](https://indiaesque.com/mumbai/heritage-guide).

sections.h2: What should you see first in Mumbai?
sections.answer: Start at the Gateway of India, at Apollo Bandar, opposite the Taj Mahal Palace hotel, and leave time to walk around Colaba. The monument is open all day and entry is free, according to [Mumbai Metro Times](https://www.mumbaimetrotimes.com/places/gateway-of-india/).
body: The Gateway of India was built between 1915 and 1924 and opened on 4 December 1924. It was designed by the Scottish architect George Wittet to commemorate the 1911 visit of King George V and Queen Mary, according to [Mumbai Metro Times](https://www.mumbaimetrotimes.com/places/gateway-of-india/).

Indiaesque describes it as a stone arch in the Indo-Saracenic style and warns that crowds are constant, so going early in the morning means fewer visitors. From there you can see the harbour and the Taj Mahal Palace hotel. [Indiaesque](https://indiaesque.com/mumbai/heritage-guide)

sections.h2: How do you get to the Elephanta Caves?
sections.answer: Boats leave from the jetties beside the Gateway of India and the crossing takes about one hour each way, according to [Indiaesque](https://indiaesque.com/mumbai/heritage-guide).
body: The caves, listed as a UNESCO site in 1987, have boats running from 9:00 to 15:30, and they are closed on Mondays and during the monsoon, the same source says. Check the day before you plan the trip. [Indiaesque](https://indiaesque.com/mumbai/heritage-guide)

The sources consulted do not name the ferry operators, so it is wise to confirm at the jetty which one is running on the day of your visit. A return trip is priced between 150 and 250 rupees, according to the same guide. [Indiaesque](https://indiaesque.com/mumbai/heritage-guide)

sections.h2: How do you get around from the center?
sections.answer: The nearest metro station is Hutatma Chowk, on Line 3 (Aqua Line), about 1.5 kilometers from the Gateway, according to [Mumbai Metro Times](https://www.mumbaimetrotimes.com/places/gateway-of-india/).
body: Local trains from Churchgate and CSMT are about 2 kilometers away, so for many visitors walking or taking a taxi from those stations is the simplest option. [Mumbai Metro Times](https://www.mumbaimetrotimes.com/places/gateway-of-india/)

The area gets busiest from 5 to 9 in the evening, according to the same page, so it is wise to plan your walk along Colaba outside that window. [Mumbai Metro Times](https://www.mumbaimetrotimes.com/places/gateway-of-india/)

sections.answer: The [Mumbai page](/destinos/in/bombay) lists the experiences you can book with Travel Puzzle. If you want to combine the city with other parts of India, write to us with your dates and we will help you put the trip together.
body: A practical order is the morning in Colaba, lunch near the port and the boat to Elephanta before the afternoon, or leaving the boat for another day if the weather does not cooperate. The monsoon closes the caves, so check the season before you choose dates.

author: editorial
enBreve: Amritsar gira en torno al Templo Dorado, un santuario sij al que se entra sin pagar. Hay que cubrir la cabeza y quitarse los zapatos, según [GoAsia](https://goasia.cc/en/article/golden-temple-amritsar). Cerca de la ciudad, la ceremonia de la frontera de Wagah es gratuita, sin reservación y dura unos 45 minutos, según [India Guide](https://india-guide.in/guides/wagah-border-guide/).

sections.h2: ¿Qué hace especial al Templo Dorado?
sections.answer: El Harmandir Sahib fue concebido como el centro de culto de los sijs por el gurú Arjan, según [GoAsia](https://goasia.cc/en/article/golden-temple-amritsar). La entrada no tiene costo y no hay restricciones por religión ni nacionalidad, de acuerdo con [Shanti Travel](https://www.shantitravel.com/en/blog/10-facts-need-know-visiting-golden-temple-amritsar.htm).
body: El complejo se describe como abierto las 24 horas, aunque el santuario interior sigue un ciclo de ceremonias: tras el cierre nocturno del Palki Sahib, hacia las 21:30 o 22:00, el acceso se pausa y vuelve a abrir entre las 2:00 y las 3:00 de la madrugada, según [Shanti Travel](https://www.shantitravel.com/en/blog/10-facts-need-know-visiting-golden-temple-amritsar.htm).

Esa misma guía fecha sus horarios en noviembre de 2024 y pide confirmarlos antes de viajar, así que tómalos como referencia. [Shanti Travel](https://www.shantitravel.com/en/blog/10-facts-need-know-visiting-golden-temple-amritsar.htm)

sections.h2: ¿Qué hay que cumplir al entrar?
sections.answer: Hay que cubrir la cabeza y quitarse los zapatos antes de entrar. En la entrada hay pañuelos para quien no traiga uno, según [Shanti Travel](https://www.shantitravel.com/en/blog/10-facts-need-know-visiting-golden-temple-amritsar.htm).
body: Antes de pasar, la misma guía recomienda lavarse los pies en las pozas designadas, como parte de la entrada al complejo.

GoAsia señala que el lugar se llena menos temprano en la mañana, sobre todo los fines de semana, así que es buen momento para llegar con calma. [GoAsia](https://goasia.cc/en/article/golden-temple-amritsar)

sections.h2: ¿Cómo funciona el langar?
sections.answer: El langar es una comida comunitaria gratuita que se sirve a todas las personas, sin importar religión, casta, credo o nacionalidad, según [GoAsia](https://goasia.cc/en/article/golden-temple-amritsar).
body: La cocina está hacia la entrada oriental del complejo y el costo lo cubren los fondos del templo, indica la misma fuente. El menú, según [Shanti Travel](https://www.shantitravel.com/en/blog/10-facts-need-know-visiting-golden-temple-amritsar.htm), es vegetariano: chapati, dal, verduras y arroz.

Shanti Travel señala que la cocina alimenta a un gran número de peregrinos, aunque sus horarios aparecen en dos versiones distintas en la misma guía, así que conviene preguntar en el lugar. [Shanti Travel](https://www.shantitravel.com/en/blog/10-facts-need-know-visiting-golden-temple-amritsar.htm)

sections.h2: ¿Qué ver en Wagah y cuándo salir?
sections.answer: La ceremonia Beating Retreat en la frontera de Wagah está a unos 30 kilómetros de Amritsar, y el trayecto dura entre 1 y 1.5 horas, según [India Guide](https://india-guide.in/guides/wagah-border-guide/).
body: La hora cambia con el atardecer. Según la misma guía, en verano la ceremonia ocurre entre las 17:15 y las 18:30 y en invierno entre las 16:00 y las 16:30, y dura unos 45 minutos. Confirma la hora en el lugar antes de salir. [India Guide](https://india-guide.in/guides/wagah-border-guide/)

Los asientos son por orden de llegada, así que conviene llegar una o dos horas antes entre semana y más temprano en fin de semana. No se permiten bolsas grandes ni power banks, y hay guardarropa cerca de la entrada, según la misma guía. [India Guide](https://india-guide.in/guides/wagah-border-guide/)

sections.h2: ¿Por qué le llaman Ciudad de la Primavera?

body: Esa temperatura templada hace cómodo caminar por la ciudad, incluso fuera de temporada. Wander in China recomienda visitarla en primavera y en otoño, cuando el clima es más agradable. [Wander in China](https://www.wanderinchina.com/destinations/kunming/)

China Explorer Tour, en cambio, indica que los meses de marzo a octubre son los más propicios para el Bosque de Piedra, y que octubre es fresco y seco, aunque también es temporada alta con más visitantes. [China Explorer Tour](https://www.chinaexplorertour.com/2026/blog/kunming-stone-forest-travel-tips-itinerary-guide/)

sections.h2: ¿Cómo llegar al Bosque de Piedra?
sections.answer: El Bosque de Piedra está a unos 88 kilómetros de la ciudad. En autobús desde la estación oriental tarda cerca de dos horas, según [China Explorer Tour](https://www.chinaexplorertour.com/2026/blog/kunming-stone-forest-travel-tips-itinerary-guide/).
body: En auto, el trayecto desde el centro dura cerca de hora y media, según la misma guía, aunque puede variar con el tráfico. [China Explorer Tour](https://www.chinaexplorertour.com/2026/blog/kunming-stone-forest-travel-tips-itinerary-guide/)

La guía también menciona el tren bala hasta Shilin West, de unos 20 minutos, y luego el autobús 99 hasta el sitio. En una tabla aparecen 30 minutos, así que conviene confirmar el tiempo antes de salir. sections.answer: La mayoría de los días se entra de 8:00 a 18:00, aunque otra sección de la misma guía da las 7:30 como hora de apertura, según [China Explorer Tour](https://www.chinaexplorertour.com/2026/blog/kunming-stone-forest-travel-tips-itinerary-guide/).

El Bosque de Piedra es un paisaje kárstico clásico, con columnas de caliza que se levantan del suelo. Por eso la visita sirve para caminar entre las formaciones sin prisa, según [China Explorer Tour](https://www.chinaexplorertour.com/2026/blog/kunming-stone-forest-travel-tips-itinerary-guide/).

en.enBreve: Kunming, in Yunnan province, is known as the City of Eternal Spring for its mild climate, according to [Wander in China](https://www.wanderinchina.com/destinations/kunming/). The Stone Forest, or Shilin, is about 88 kilometers away and takes roughly two hours by bus, according to [China Explorer Tour](https://www.chinaexplorertour.com/2026/blog/kunming-stone-forest-travel-tips-itinerary-guide/).

sections.h2: Why is it called the City of Spring?
sections.answer: Kunming has a mild climate almost all year, with average temperatures of about 15 to 24 degrees Celsius, according to [Wander in China](https://www.wanderinchina.com/destinations/kunming/).
body: That mild temperature makes it comfortable to walk around the city, even outside peak season. Wander in China recommends visiting in spring and autumn, when the weather is most pleasant. [Wander in China](https://www.wanderinchina.com/destinations/kunming/)

China Explorer Tour, on the other hand, says March through October is the most suitable period for the Stone Forest, and that October is cool and dry but also a busy season with more visitors. [China Explorer Tour](https://www.chinaexplorertour.com/2026/blog/kunming-stone-forest-travel-tips-itinerary-guide/)

sections.h2: How do you get to the Stone Forest?
sections.answer: The Stone Forest is about 88 kilometers from the city. By bus from the East Coach Station it takes close to two hours, according to [China Explorer Tour](https://www.chinaexplorertour.com/2026/blog/kunming-stone-forest-travel-tips-itinerary-guide/).
body: By car, the trip from downtown takes about an hour and a half, according to the same guide, although traffic can change that. [China Explorer Tour](https://www.chinaexplorertour.com/2026/blog/kunming-stone-forest-travel-tips-itinerary-guide/)

The guide also mentions the bullet train to Shilin West, about 20 minutes, and then bus 99 to the site. A table in it lists 30 minutes, so it is wise to confirm the time before you leave. [China Explorer Tour](https://www.chinaexplorertour.com/2026/blog/kunming-stone-forest-travel-tips-itinerary-guide/)

sections.h2: What are the opening hours and how are tickets bought?
sections.answer: Most days you can enter from 8:00 to 18:00, although another section of the same guide gives 7:30 as the opening time, according to [China Explorer Tour](https://www.chinaexplorertour.com/2026/blog/kunming-stone-forest-travel-tips-itinerary-guide/).
body: Tickets can be bought at the entrance or online, and prices may change. Students, seniors and children may get discounts, the same guide says. [China Explorer Tour](https://www.chinaexplorertour.com/2026/blog/kunming-stone-forest-travel-tips-itinerary-guide/)

The Stone Forest is a classic karst landscape, with limestone columns rising from the ground. That is why a visit works well for walking among the formations at an unhurried pace, according to [China Explorer Tour](https://www.chinaexplorertour.com/2026/blog/kunming-stone-forest-travel-tips-itinerary-guide/).

sections.h2: What else is there in Kunming?
sections.answer: Besides the forest, the [Wander in China](https://www.wanderinchina.com/destinations/kunming/) guide mentions Dianchi Lake, Green Lake Park and the Western Hills, although it does not describe them in detail.
body: The Kunming City Museum appears as an option in the same guide. There are no distances or opening hours listed for these places, so it is wise to confirm them before you go. [Wander in China](https://www.wanderinchina.com/destinations/kunming/)

sections.answer: The [Kunming page](/destinos/cn/kunming) lists the experiences you can book with Travel Puzzle. If you want to combine Kunming with other cities in China, write to us with your dates and we will help you put the trip together.
body: Because the forest means a long round trip, the practical choice is to book it as a full-day outing and keep the other days in the city for the parks and the lake.

titulo: Guía de Singapur: Gardens by the Bay, los Supertrees y cómo entrar al país
author: editorial
enBreve: Singapur se recorre bien en tres o cuatro días. Para turismo, quienes tienen pasaporte mexicano no necesitan visa y pueden quedarse hasta 30 días, según [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visa_requirements_for_Mexican_citizens). Gardens by the Bay, junto a Marina Bay, reúne dos invernaderos y los Supertrees iluminados, según [Singapore Spirit](https://www.singapore-spirit.com/guides/gardens-by-the-bay-guide/).

sections.h2: ¿Necesitan visa los mexicanos para entrar?
sections.answer: Para turismo no se pide visa a quienes tienen pasaporte mexicano, y pueden permanecer hasta 30 días, según [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visa_requirements_for_Mexican_citizens).
body: Antes de llegar conviene enviar la SG Arrival Card, que se presenta en línea junto con la declaración electrónica de salud, según la [ICA](https://www.ica.gov.sg/enter-transit-depart/entering-singapore/sg-arrival-card).

El trámite es gratuito, y la ICA indica que no respalda a las empresas que cobran por enviarla en nombre de quien viaja. Conviene hacerlo directamente en el sitio oficial. [ICA](https://www.ica.gov.sg/enter-transit-depart/entering-singapore/sg-arrival-card)

sections.h2: ¿Qué ver en Gardens by the Bay?
sections.answer: El complejo tiene el Cloud Forest, un invernadero con una montaña artificial de 35 metros y una cascada de 30, y el Flower Dome, que la guía describe como el invernadero de vidrio más grande del mundo por volumen, según [Singapore Spirit](https://www.singapore-spirit.com/guides/gardens-by-the-bay-guide/).
body: El Cloud Forest recrea un ambiente de montaña tropical entre 1,000 y 3,500 metros de altura, y su boleto para adultos cuesta 26 dólares de Singapur. Los dos invernaderos juntos cuestan 46 dólares de Singapur, según [Singapore Spirit](https://www.singapore-spirit.com/guides/gardens-by-the-bay-guide/).

La Supertree Grove al aire libre es gratuita y tiene 18 estructuras verticales de entre 25 y 50 metros, cubiertas de plantas y encendidas de noche, según [Singapore Spirit](https://www.singapore-spirit.com/guides/gardens-by-the-bay-guide/).

sections.h2: ¿Cuándo es el show de luces y cómo llegar?
sections.answer: El show Garden Rhapsody se proyecta sobre los Supertrees cada noche a las 19:45 y a las 20:45, sin boleto, según [Singapore Spirit](https://www.singapore-spirit.com/guides/gardens-by-the-bay-guide/).
body: En fines de semana el área al aire libre se llena desde cerca de las 19:15, así que conviene llegar temprano para elegir lugar con calma. [Singapore Spirit](https://www.singapore-spirit.com/guides/gardens-by-the-bay-guide/)

Para llegar, toma el MRT a la estación Bayfront (CE1/DT16), que es un cruce de las líneas Circle y Downtown. Desde la salida B hay un paso subterráneo hacia Marina Bay Sands, y de ahí el recorrido a pie dura de 10 a 15 minutos, según [Singapore Spirit](https://www.singapore-spirit.com/guides/gardens-by-the-bay-guide/).

sections.answer: En la [página de Singapur](/destinos/sg/singapur) están las experiencias que puedes reservar con Travel Puzzle. Si quieres combinar la ciudad con otros destinos del sudeste asiático, escríbenos con tus fechas y te ayudamos a armar el viaje.
body: Un buen orden es dejar Gardens by the Bay para la tarde y la noche, y reservar la mañana para moverte entre barrios o visitar otra parte de la ciudad. Así llegas al show sin prisa.

en.titulo: Singapore guide: Gardens by the Bay, the Supertrees and how to enter the country
en.enBreve: Singapore is easy to cover in three or four days. For tourism, holders of Mexican passports do not need a visa and can stay up to 30 days, according to [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visa_requirements_for_Mexican_citizens). Gardens by the Bay, next to Marina Bay, combines two conservatories and the illuminated Supertrees, according to [Singapore Spirit](https://www.singapore-spirit.com/guides/gardens-by-the-bay-guide/).

sections.h2: Do Mexicans need a visa to enter?
sections.answer: For tourism, no visa is required for holders of Mexican passports, who can stay up to 30 days, according to [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visa_requirements_for_Mexican_citizens).
body: Before arriving, it is wise to submit the SG Arrival Card, which is filed online together with the electronic health declaration, according to the [ICA](https://www.ica.gov.sg/enter-transit-depart/entering-singapore/sg-arrival-card).

Submitting it is free, and the ICA states that it does not support businesses that charge a fee to submit it on behalf of travelers. It is best to file it directly on the official site. [ICA](https://www.ica.gov.sg/enter-transit-depart/entering-singapore/sg-arrival-card)

sections.h2: What is there to see at Gardens by the Bay?
sections.answer: The complex has the Cloud Forest, a conservatory with a 35-meter artificial mountain and a 30-meter waterfall, and the Flower Dome, which the guide describes as the world's largest glass greenhouse by volume, according to [Singapore Spirit](https://www.singapore-spirit.com/guides/gardens-by-the-bay-guide/).
body: The Cloud Forest recreates a tropical mountain environment between 1,000 and 3,500 meters in elevation, and the adult ticket costs 26 Singapore dollars. Both conservatories together cost 46 Singapore dollars, according to [Singapore Spirit](https://www.singapore-spirit.com/guides/gardens-by-the-bay-guide/).

The outdoor Supertree Grove is free to enter and has 18 vertical structures between 25 and 50 meters tall, covered in plants and lit up at night, according to [Singapore Spirit](https://www.singapore-spirit.com/guides/gardens-by-the-bay-guide/).

sections.h2: When is the light show and how do you get there?
sections.answer: The Garden Rhapsody show is projected onto the Supertrees every night at 19:45 and 20:45, with no ticket required, according to [Singapore Spirit](https://www.singapore-spirit.com/guides/gardens-by-the-bay-guide/).
body: On weekends the outdoor area fills up from around 19:15, so it is wise to arrive early and pick a spot at a relaxed pace. [Singapore Spirit](https://www.singapore-spirit.com/guides/gardens-by-the-bay-guide/)

To get there, take the MRT to Bayfront station (CE1/DT16), where the Circle and Downtown lines meet. From exit B an underground passage leads to Marina Bay Sands, and the walk from there takes 10 to 15 minutes, according to [Singapore Spirit](https://www.singapore-spirit.com/guides/gardens-by-the-bay-guide/).

body: A good order is to leave Gardens by the Bay for the afternoon and evening, and use the morning to move between neighborhoods or visit another part of the city. That way you reach the show without rushing.
